nodes.name: Visual Arts
nodes.description: Art forms appreciated primarily through sight, encompassing painting, sculpture, drawing, printmaking, photography, and calligraphy.

nodes.name: Painting
nodes.description: The application of pigment to a surface to create an image.

nodes.name: Oil Painting
nodes.description: Painting with pigments suspended in drying oils, dominant in Western art since the Renaissance.

nodes.name: Watercolor
nodes.description: Painting with pigments suspended in a water-soluble binder, valued for transparency.

nodes.name: Gouache
nodes.description: Opaque watercolor paint producing a matte finish.

nodes.name: Acrylic Painting
nodes.description: Fast-drying painting with synthetic polymer pigments.

nodes.name: Tempera
nodes.description: Painting with pigment bound in egg yolk or other emulsion.

nodes.name: Fresco
nodes.description: Mural painting on fresh lime plaster so pigment bonds as it dries.

nodes.name: Encaustic Painting
nodes.description: Painting with pigments suspended in heated beeswax.

nodes.name: Pastel Painting
nodes.description: Painting with sticks of pure powdered pigment and binder.

nodes.name: Spray Painting
nodes.description: Applying paint through aerosol or airbrush, central to graffiti and street art.

nodes.name: Cave Painting
nodes.description: Prehistoric paintings on cave walls, among the earliest known art.

nodes.name: Portrait Painting
nodes.description: Painting depicting a specific person or group.

nodes.name: Landscape Painting
nodes.description: Painting of natural scenery as its principal subject.

nodes.name: Still Life
nodes.description: Painting of inanimate objects arranged as a composition.

nodes.name: History Painting
nodes.description: Large-scale painting of historical, mythological, or biblical narratives.

nodes.name: Genre Painting
nodes.description: Painting of scenes of everyday life.

nodes.name: Figure Painting
nodes.description: Painting centered on the human figure.

nodes.name: Abstract Painting
nodes.description: Non-representational painting using form, color, and gesture.

nodes.name: Mural Painting
nodes.description: Large-scale painting executed directly on walls or ceilings.

nodes.name: Miniature Painting
nodes.description: Small detailed painting, especially of Persian, Mughal, and medieval traditions.

nodes.name: Icon Painting
nodes.description: Sacred panel painting of Orthodox Christian tradition.

nodes.name: Trompe-l'oeil
nodes.description: Illusionistic painting that deceives the eye into seeing real objects.

nodes.name: Ink Wash Painting
nodes.description: East Asian monochrome painting in ink applied with brush and water.

nodes.name: Chinese Ink Painting
nodes.description: The Chinese tradition of brush-and-ink painting, including shan shui landscapes.

nodes.name: Sumi-e
nodes.description: Japanese ink wash painting emphasizing simplicity and empty space.

nodes.name: Drawing
nodes.description: Mark-making with dry or wet media on a surface, the foundation of many visual arts.

nodes.name: Pencil Drawing
nodes.description: Drawing with graphite pencils in a range of hardnesses.

nodes.name: Charcoal Drawing
nodes.description: Drawing with burnt wood sticks for rich dark tones.

nodes.name: Pen and Ink
nodes.description: Drawing with ink applied by pen, often with hatching and stippling.

nodes.name: Pastel Drawing
nodes.description: Drawing with sticks of pigment, spanning dry and oil pastels.

nodes.name: Silverpoint
nodes.description: Drawing with a silver wire on prepared ground, used in the Renaissance.

nodes.name: Figure Drawing
nodes.description: Drawing the human form, often from life.

nodes.name: Life Drawing
nodes.description: Drawing from a live model to study anatomy and gesture.

nodes.name: Sketching
nodes.description: Rapid informal drawing to capture ideas or observations.

nodes.name: Sculpture
nodes.description: Three-dimensional art created by carving, modeling, casting, or assembling materials.

nodes.name: Carving
nodes.description: Subtractive sculpture by cutting away material from stone or wood.

nodes.name: Modeling
nodes.description: Additive sculpture by shaping pliable material such as clay or wax.

nodes.name: Casting
nodes.description: Producing sculpture by pouring molten material into a mold.

nodes.name: Assemblage
nodes.description: Sculpture assembled from found objects and mixed materials.

nodes.name: Relief Sculpture
nodes.description: Sculpture projecting from a flat background surface.

nodes.name: Stone Sculpture
nodes.description: Sculpture carved from stone such as marble, granite, or limestone.

nodes.name: Bronze Sculpture
nodes.description: Sculpture cast in bronze, valued for durability and detail.

nodes.name: Wood Sculpture
nodes.description: Sculpture carved or assembled from wood.

nodes.name: Kinetic Sculpture
nodes.description: Sculpture incorporating movement, whether motorized or wind-driven.

nodes.name: Statue
nodes.description: A free-standing representational sculpture of a figure.

nodes.name: Bust
nodes.description: A sculpture of a person's head, shoulders, and chest.

nodes.name: Installation Art
nodes.description: Immersive art occupying a space, engaging the viewer's environment.

nodes.name: Printmaking
nodes.description: Creating artworks by transferring ink from a prepared matrix to paper or other support.

nodes.name: Relief Printing
nodes.description: Printing from raised areas of a carved block.

nodes.name: Woodcut
nodes.description: Relief print from a carved wood block.

nodes.name: Linocut
nodes.description: Relief print from a carved linoleum block.

nodes.name: Intaglio
nodes.description: Printing from ink held in incised lines of a plate.

nodes.name: Engraving
nodes.description: Intaglio print from lines cut into a metal plate with a burin.

nodes.name: Etching
nodes.description: Intaglio print from a metal plate bitten by acid through a resist.

nodes.name: Drypoint
nodes.description: Intaglio print from lines scratched directly into a plate.

nodes.name: Mezzotint
nodes.description: Intaglio technique producing rich tonal gradations.

nodes.name: Lithography
nodes.description: Planographic printing from a stone or plate using grease-and-water repulsion.

nodes.name: Screen Printing
nodes.description: Printing by forcing ink through a stencil on a mesh screen.

nodes.name: Monoprint
nodes.description: A one-off print made from a plate without a repeatable edition.

nodes.name: Photography
nodes.description: Creating images by recording light, whether chemically or digitally.

nodes.name: Portrait Photography
nodes.description: Photography of people, capturing likeness and character.

nodes.name: Landscape Photography
nodes.description: Photography of natural and urban scenery.

nodes.name: Documentary Photography
nodes.description: Photography recording events and conditions to inform or witness.

nodes.name: Street Photography
nodes.description: Candid photography of public spaces and everyday life.

nodes.name: Fine Art Photography
nodes.description: Photography created as aesthetic expression rather than documentation.

nodes.name: Still Life Photography
nodes.description: Photography of arranged inanimate objects.

nodes.name: War Photography
nodes.description: Photography documenting armed conflict and its human cost.

nodes.name: Wildlife Photography
nodes.description: Photography of animals in their natural habitats.

nodes.name: Architectural Photography
nodes.description: Photography of buildings and built structures.

nodes.name: Macro Photography
nodes.description: Extreme close-up photography of small subjects.

nodes.name: Astrophotography
nodes.description: Photography of astronomical objects and the night sky.

nodes.name: Black-and-White Photography
nodes.description: Monochrome photography emphasizing tone, form, and contrast.

nodes.name: Long Exposure Photography
nodes.description: Photography using extended shutter times to blur motion or gather light.

nodes.name: Calligraphy
nodes.description: The art of beautiful writing executed with a brush or pen.

nodes.name: Chinese Calligraphy
nodes.description: The brush-written art of Chinese characters, central to East Asian literati culture.

nodes.name: Japanese Calligraphy
nodes.description: The Japanese art of writing with brush and ink, known as shodo.

nodes.name: Korean Calligraphy
nodes.description: The Korean brush-writing tradition of Hanja and Hangul.

nodes.name: Islamic Calligraphy
nodes.description: The calligraphic art of Arabic script, central to Islamic art.

nodes.name: Western Calligraphy
nodes.description: The Latin-script tradition of formal penmanship and illuminated writing.

nodes.name: Illustration
nodes.description: Art created to clarify, decorate, or accompany text and ideas.

nodes.name: Editorial Illustration
nodes.description: Illustration accompanying magazine, newspaper, and online articles.

nodes.name: Children's Book Illustration
nodes.description: Illustration for picture books and children's literature.

nodes.name: Scientific Illustration
nodes.description: Precise depiction of scientific subjects for research and education.

nodes.name: Botanical Illustration
nodes.description: Accurate depiction of plants for scientific and horticultural records.

nodes.name: Medical Illustration
nodes.description: Depiction of anatomy and procedures for medical education.

nodes.name: Fashion Illustration
nodes.description: Drawing of garments and looks to communicate fashion design.

nodes.name: Collage
nodes.description: Art assembled by gluing diverse materials onto a surface.

nodes.name: Mixed Media
nodes.description: Art combining multiple distinct media within one work.

nodes.name: Mosaic
nodes.description: Images formed by assembling small pieces of stone, glass, or tile.

nodes.name: Stained Glass
nodes.description: Colored glass assembled into pictorial windows, chiefly in churches.

nodes.name: Street Art
nodes.description: Art created in public spaces, encompassing graffiti, murals, and installations.

nodes.name: Graffiti
nodes.description: Writing or drawing made illicitly on walls and surfaces.

nodes.name: Stencil Art
nodes.description: Street art produced by spraying through cut stencils.

nodes.name: Muralism
nodes.description: Large public murals, especially the Mexican mural movement of the 1920s.

nodes.name: Renaissance Art
nodes.description: European art of the 14th-17th centuries reviving classical ideals, perspective, and humanism.

nodes.name: Baroque Art
nodes.description: Dramatic, dynamic European art of the 17th century emphasizing motion and emotion.

nodes.name: Rococo
nodes.description: Ornamental, playful 18th-century art with light colors and asymmetry.

nodes.name: Neoclassicism
nodes.description: Late 18th-century art reviving Greco-Roman forms and moral austerity.

nodes.name: Romanticism
nodes.description: Early 19th-century art exalting emotion, nature, and the sublime.

nodes.name: Realism
nodes.description: Mid-19th-century art depicting ordinary life without idealization.

nodes.name: Impressionism
nodes.description: Late 19th-century art capturing fleeting light and color in loose brushwork.

nodes.name: Post-Impressionism
nodes.description: Late 19th-century art extending Impressionism toward structure and expression.

nodes.name: Expressionism
nodes.description: Early 20th-century art distorting form to convey subjective emotion.

nodes.name: Fauvism
nodes.description: Early 20th-century painting with bold, arbitrary color.

nodes.name: Cubism
nodes.description: Early 20th-century art fragmenting form into geometric planes.

nodes.name: Futurism
nodes.description: Early 20th-century Italian movement celebrating speed, technology, and dynamism.

nodes.name: Dada
nodes.description: Anti-art movement of the 1910s-20s rejecting reason and convention.

nodes.name: Surrealism
nodes.description: 20th-century art exploring dreams and the unconscious through unexpected juxtaposition.

nodes.name: Abstract Expressionism
nodes.description: Mid-20th-century American painting emphasizing gesture, scale, and spontaneity.

nodes.name: Pop Art
nodes.description: Art of the 1950s-60s drawing on mass media and consumer culture.

nodes.name: Op Art
nodes.description: Art using optical illusions and geometric pattern.

nodes.name: Minimalism
nodes.description: Mid-20th-century art reducing form to essential geometric elements.

nodes.name: Conceptual Art
nodes.description: Art in which the idea takes precedence over the physical object.

nodes.name: Land Art
nodes.description: Art made in and from the landscape, often monumental and site-specific.

nodes.name: Arte Povera
nodes.description: 1960s Italian movement using humble, everyday materials.

nodes.name: Fluxus
nodes.description: Interdisciplinary 1960s movement blending art, music, and performance.

nodes.name: Art Nouveau
nodes.description: Ornamental late 19th-century style with flowing organic lines.

nodes.name: Art Deco
nodes.description: Elegant 1920s-30s style of geometric forms and luxurious materials.

nodes.name: De Stijl
nodes.description: Dutch movement reducing art to horizontal and vertical lines and primary colors.

nodes.name: Constructivism
nodes.description: Russian avant-garde movement uniting art with industrial production.

nodes.name: Suprematism
nodes.description: Russian movement of pure geometric abstraction founded by Malevich.

nodes.name: Bauhaus
nodes.description: German school and movement uniting art, craft, and industrial design.

nodes.name: Symbolism
nodes.description: Late 19th-century art expressing ideas through symbols and mood.

nodes.name: Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood
nodes.description: 19th-century English movement rejecting academic convention for medieval detail and color.

nodes.name: Ukiyo-e
nodes.description: Japanese woodblock prints and paintings of the floating world, 17th-19th centuries.

nodes.name: Social Realism
nodes.description: Art depicting working-class life to provoke social awareness.

nodes.name: Naive Art
nodes.description: Art by self-taught artists with childlike simplicity.

nodes.name: Outsider Art
nodes.description: Art made outside the mainstream, often by self-taught or institutionalized artists.
